study_identification.title: Dissecting heterogeneity in major depressive disorder via normative model-driven subtyping of functional brain networks

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: - One-sample t-tests on ROI deviations per subtype to classify regions as positively/negatively deviating; Pearson correlations between deviation values and HAMD-17 scores with Bonferroni/FDR correction. - Two-sample t-tests to compare network-level mean deviations between subtypes; significant differences across VIS/SMN/VAN (higher in Subtype 2) and LIM/FPN/DMN (lower in Subtype 2). - PLS regression linking deviation maps to Neurosynth-derived cognitive terms, with permutation testing and bootstrapped weights.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Normative modeling of rs-fMRI degree centrality revealed two MDD subtypes with opposing deviation patterns between unimodal (VIS/SMN) and transmodal (LIM/FPN/DMN) networks, accompanied by distinct cognitive associations and clinical differences.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: From 797 MDD and 822 HC (REST-meta-MDD), HBR normative models (PCNtoolkit v0.28) produced ROI-wise deviation z-scores (|z| ≥ 2.6 as outliers). K-means clustering (k=2) on deviation profiles yielded Subtype 1 (N=438) and Subtype 2 (N=359). Subtype 1 showed negative deviations in VIS/SMN and positive deviations in VAN/LIM/FPN/DMN; Subtype 2 showed the reverse. Network-level differences were significant (e.g., VIS: t=11.178, p<0.001; SMN: t=23.733, p<0.001; VAN: t=3.056, p=0.003; LIM: t=17.666, p<0.001; FPN: t=9.351, p<0.001; DMN: t=18.353, p<0.001). HAMD-17 subscale differences included higher General Somatic Symptoms and Hypochondriasis in Subtype 2 (p=0.031; p=0.023). CV on HC showed SMSE≈1.014±0.005 and MSLL≈0.001±0.004, indicating good model fit.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional design limits causal and longitudinal inference; no external dataset for validation; incomplete clinical data for some patients (episode status, medication) may constrain analyses; cognitive mapping was at the group level rather than individual-level links.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: - Neurosynth-based cognitive mapping via PLS links subtype-specific deviations to cognitive functions. - Cross-atlas validation (Harvard–Oxford vs AAL90) showed high consistency and similar clustering (overlap~0.726). - Subtype deviation patterns were robust to medication and episode status (no significant differences within subgroups).

general_notes.general_notes: - Sites 4 and 25 excluded (duplication; late-onset/remitted). - Sites with <10 MDD or <10 HC excluded to ensure adequate per-site samples. - QC thresholds included mean FD>0.2 mm and visual QC for distortions/signal loss. - Graph thresholds: sparsity 0.05–0.50 step 0.01; ROI assignment to Yeo 7 networks by voxel majority. - Validation metrics reported for HC CV (SMSE, MSLL) with distribution plots in Supplementary Fig S2. - Proportions of positive/negative ROI outliers across MDD ranged roughly 0.13–1.95% depending on region.
